calls.reasoning: Base rate: since the Apr 8 ceasefire, qualifying US strikes on Iranian land or territorial waters happened in only one ~8-day cluster (Sept 1-8). That is about 1 of 7-8 comparable 24-day windows, roughly 13-15%. The status quo is no US strike since Sept 8, with Hormuz talks ongoing. Factors pushing up: the bar is low, since one tanker strike in Kharg waters counts. US tanker flights surged (82 on Oct 1-14 against 98 in all of August), troop levels are rising again, Iranian officials expect imminent strikes, Netanyahu is reportedly pushing for strikes before end-October, and the window runs 6 days past the Nov 3 midterms. Factors pushing down: Washington reportedly rules out any operation before Nov 3. The third carrier and its air wing only arrive in late November, after the window, so a planned major campaign most likely starts after Nov 10. Munitions stocks are reported to be low. Small opportunistic strikes, such as enforcement action against tankers or retaliation, remain the main way this resolves Yes.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs drew on the same evidence: the question background plus one Oct 14 La Voix du Nord/i24news digest. Their web tools failed, and I had no web access on this run either. They agree on every factual claim: the September strike dates, the counts of tanker flights, the reported US position of no operation before Nov 3, the late-November carrier arrival, and no reported strikes since Sept 8. The only factual open question is whether any US strikes on Iran happened during the summer 'low-level conflict', which would raise the base rate. None of the runs could confirm it, and the background lists only the three September strikes as qualifying, so I keep the base rate around 13-15% and treat this as a small upside uncertainty. The rest is judgment: how far the October buildup and Iranian alarm should move the estimate up from the base rate, against the US 'not before the election' stance and the carrier timeline pointing to a campaign after Nov 10. I read the buildup as preparation for a campaign that most likely starts after the window. Within the window, the realistic paths to Yes are an opportunistic small strike or a short campaign launched on Nov 4-9, so I land slightly below the runs, at 0.28. I found no matching human market.
